messages.subject: fpeaks issue when creating data frame
messages.subject_clean: fpeaks issue when creating data frame
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am new to R and I'm trying to find the number of peaks for ~2000 1 minute wav files. When I run my script to find the peaks and create a .csv with columns of peaknumber, filename, freq and amp. What is happening is that at certain peaks possibly relating to the amp being 1, the next row is messed up with the peaknumer containing the word freq, and the same frequency coordinate having multiple amplitudes. Furthermore the peaknumber column is then corrupted. After a certain time R will give the error that the arguments imply different numbers of rows (somehow the 2 column fpeaks object is making extra rows for 1 or more of the data frame columns). I have tried changing the amp argument for fpeaks to 0 on the right side of the peak. The script will run without stopping due to an error however the output .csv still has the same problems. Here is my script and I've attached a screenshot of whats happening in the .csv.

   # Calculate mean frequency spectrum, find and select peaks and save output for all wav files in directory

    files <- list.files ()          # Make a list of all wav files in  working dir
    n <- length (files)                             # number of files
    n

    peaks <- data.frame()  # Creates empty dataframe, where results will be stored

    # Loop to detect, select peaks and stored output
    for(i in files) {
      wave <- readWave (filename = i, from =0, to=60, units = "seconds")
      temp <- meanspec(wave, f = 44100, plot = FALSE, identify = TRUE)                      # calculate mean frequency spectrum
      peaks_temp <- fpeaks(temp, amp=c(0.01,0.01), freq=200, plot = FALSE)                  # detect and select peaks with specific attributes
      peaks <- rbind (peaks,  data.frame(i, freq = peaks_temp[, 1], amp = peaks_temp[, 2])) # save output
    }

    # change name of colun named 'I' to 'FILENAME'
    names(peaks)[names(peaks) =='i']<- 'FILENAME'

    # Add columns to output indicating Location
    Location <- c("SDF")

    peaks <- cbind (peaks, Location)

    # Saves output in working directory
    write.csv (peaks, "D:/R/Results/temp/NP/peaks_site1.csv")

    rm(list=ls())

All help very appreciated!

Best,
Rory MacGregor

messages.subject: Splliting a spectrogram
messages.body_plain:
Hi jérôme,

We want to split a spectrogram such that we get one spectrogram per syllable of a sound (we have the syllables coordinates).

We used "spectro" function with the option "tlim" and the syllables coordinates. It works but... it turns out that these "local" spectrograms are not exactly the same that when we plot the whole spectrogram... In other word, looking at the whole spectrogram or looking at a local spectrogram, we don't have the same image...

Is there a way to obtain exactly the same spectrogram image when we look at the whole or part of the spectrogram?

Many thanks, et merci

Vincent M, LBBE LYON
